phase: DRP3 / DRP12 gate — the RESIDENT Airflow deployment emits OpenLineage
verdict: LIVE PASS — unconditional. This supersedes the earlier isolated-pod evidence.
what_changed: scripts/airflow-enable-lineage.sh --execute rolled Helm revision 2: image airflow-openlineage:3.2.2-ol2.20.2 and the four AIRFLOW__OPENLINEAGE__* variables the deployed release had never carried.

evidence.method: real DAG run through KubernetesExecutor; three worker pods; logs scraped while the pods were alive
evidence.ownership: data-platform — the DAG's real owner, carried through to the event
evidence.documentation: Connector liveness, topic flow and source-position advance — the DAG's real docstring

note_on_the_FAIL: the task itself failed (a connector liveness probe; the CDC runtime is not currently serving). That is unrelated to lineage and PRE-EXISTING. It is in fact stronger evidence: FAIL events emit too, so a failing task is not invisible to the lineage graph.

attempts_that_did_not_work_and_why.attempt: write a probe DAG onto the dags PVC
attempts_that_did_not_work_and_why.result: Permission denied — the PVC is not writable from the pod

attempts_that_did_not_work_and_why.attempt: airflow dags test in the SCHEDULER
attempts_that_did_not_work_and_why.result: Dag could not be found — in Airflow 3 only the dag-processor mounts the dags volume

attempts_that_did_not_work_and_why.attempt: airflow dags test in the DAG-PROCESSOR
attempts_that_did_not_work_and_why.result: exit 137, OOM-killed: the container is limited to 512Mi and the Airflow 3.2.2 task SDK needs more. The listener WAS active — it logged its emission policy for the task before the kill.
exit 137 as well — the limit binds on import, not on the task

operational_notes: there is NO remote logging configured, so worker-pod logs are lost when the pod is deleted (delete_worker_pods defaults to true). Capturing lineage from task logs requires scraping while the pod lives, or enabling remote logging.
the DAG was re-paused after the run; it was paused before.
cost: $0 — one DAG run on an already-running cluster
